The strongest text-grounded reading shows no conflict relation. A constrains a Parameter Object’s name field to match a template expression in the associated path. B constrains patterned fields to have unique names within their containing object. Even if one assumes overlap, these are different constraint dimensions: path-correspondence versus intra-object uniqueness. Nothing in either text requires duplicate names, forbids path-matching names from being unique, or otherwise obstructs joint satisfaction. The only ambiguity is whether the same field is covered by both, but that ambiguity does not create interference, inconsistency, or impossible joint satisfaction.

The pair does not establish a text-grounded conflict. Requirement A constrains a Parameter Object’s name field so it matches a template expression in an associated path. Requirement B constrains Paths Object field names to start with an alphanumeric character. Even if the associated path in A is a Paths Object field name, the constraints act on different properties of that path context: A on parameter/template correspondence, B on lexical starting character. No interference, inconsistency, or no-solution condition is forced by the text; both can be satisfied together (e.g., an alphanumeric-starting path key containing a template expression matched by the parameter name).

The pair is loosely anchored to the same domain—path-related parameters—but not to the same constraint dimension. A requires that a Parameter Object used in the path have a name matching a template expression in that path. B governs whether Path Item–level parameters may be overridden or removed at the Operation level. These prescriptions do not obstruct each other, do not state conflicting conditions, and can be jointly satisfied: an overridden parameter can still comply with A, and B says nothing that negates A’s naming rule.
